tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the websites on this DevDome account with their verification status.

tools.name: add_site
tools.description: Add a website to the account. Returns the verification file to upload (verify_file_path + verify_content, served at /.well-known/devdome-analytics.txt); the site stays pending until verified.

tools.name: verify_site
tools.description: Verify ownership of a pending website (checks the installed snippet or DNS TXT record).

tools.name: get_stats
tools.description: Headline KPIs for a site as raw counts: visits, visitors, pageviews, clicks (outbound), bots, bounces, session_seconds, dur_sessions, each for the current and the previous period. Derive the rates yourself the way the dashboard does: bounce rate = bounces / visits; average visit duration = session_s

tools.name: get_timeseries
tools.description: Daily traffic series for a site (visits, visitors, pageviews, clicks, bots per day, in the site's timezone). Window by days, or from and to (YYYY-MM-DD); omit both for the full history the plan retains.

tools.name: get_breakdown
tools.description: Top-N breakdown of a site's traffic by one dimension. regions needs country (ISO alpha-2); cities needs country and takes region. countries / regions / cities ignore the page, referrer, campaign, event and goal filters (they are the country-scoped views themselves).

tools.name: get_bot_report
tools.description: Bot traffic on a site - DevDome separates every hit into human vs bot. kind 'bots' = known-bot catalog activity; 'threats' = suspicious/behavioral detections.

tools.name: get_realtime
tools.description: Visitors active on the site in the last 5 minutes, with their current page and path.

tools.name: get_visitors
tools.description: Recent individual visits: entry page, path taken, country, device, human/bot.

tools.name: get_site_health
tools.description: Uptime/health summary for a site: status, response time, TLS/domain checks, open incidents, the latest daily audit (DNS, certificate, security headers, SEO basics, tracker) and the Malware Scanner roll-up. Compact: the raw 24h probe list and the scanner file list are left out (the dashboard has them

tools.name: get_hourly
tools.description: The last 24 hours by hour (UTC timestamps): visits, visitors, pageviews, clicks, bots per hour. Fixed window, no days/from/to.

tools.name: get_paths
tools.description: The visitors who ENTERED the site on one page, each with the step-by-step path they took afterwards. page = the entry page path, e.g. /pricing.

tools.name: get_incidents
tools.description: Downtime incidents of a site, newest first, with start, end, confirmation time, failing status and category. Pages: when has_more is true, pass the started_at of the last row as before.

tools.name: get_goals
tools.description: The site's saved goals (Website Settings > Goals) with how many human and bot visitors completed each one in the window: type page (a path, * = any part), click (an outbound destination), event (a custom event name) or scroll (a scroll depth percent). Each row carries the goal id for the goal filter

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: Custom events the site sends (devdome('event', name) or the plugin's event tracking): one row per event name with counts for the window. Event names feed the event filter.

tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Live DNS and domain checks for ANY public domain (not only account sites): dns = records of one type (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, CAA; default A), mx / ns / txt = that record set, email_auth = SPF + DMARC + DKIM (common selectors, or dkim_selector), whois = registrar, status and expiry from th

tools.name: check_url
tools.description: Live HTTP check of ANY public https URL from Cloudflare's network: status = status code, final URL, response time and the main response headers; redirects = the hop-by-hop redirect chain (up to 10 hops) with each status and location; security_headers = the DevDome security-header audit of that URL (

tools.name: lookup_bot
tools.description: Is this user-agent string a known bot or crawler, and which one: matched against DevDome's bot catalog (AI crawlers, search engines, SEO tools, monitors) and the live crawler feed the analytics use. tools.description: Generate a ready-to-use file or link, the same output as the free DevDome tools, nothing fetched or stored: robots_txt = a WordPress robots.txt from a preset (standard, woo, ai, privacy) or a rules list (admin, ajax, rest, search, feeds, trackbacks, woo, ai_training, ai_search) with an optional site

findings.detail: Description of "get_stats" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.detail: Description of "get_stats" is 1032 chars, far longer than this server's median (197). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "generate_file" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: kind, preset, rules, sitemap_url, redirects, code, domain, www, force_https, trailing_slash, wordpress_block, url, source, medium, campaign, id, term, content, normalize, title, summary, details, sections, optional

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_events, check_url, lookup_bot, inspect_page, generate_file · Private data: add_site, verify_site, get_site_health, check_domain, generate_file · Public sink: add_site.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_events, check_url, lookup_bot, inspect_page, generate_file · Private data: add_site, verify_site, get_site_health, check_domain, generate_file · Public sink: add_site

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
